key_insight: This paper develops a physics-guided diffusion model to forecast detailed floodwater depths over four days. It targets a less computationally demanding alternative to full physics simulations, though the provided abstract does not report performance results.
problem_solved: High-resolution flood forecasting with two-dimensional shallow water equation solvers is computationally expensive, even on GPUs.
method: Use a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model to forecast evolving water-depth fields at 30 m resolution.
Train on SynxFlow shallow water simulations of 113 historical storms observed across twelve Midwestern states from 2003–2024.
Apply the model to four-day flood forecasting in Illinois’s Des Plaines River watershed; the excerpt does not specify how physics guidance is implemented.
impact: The approach explores diffusion models as surrogates for costly environmental simulations. For AI/ML practitioners, it offers a physics-guided spatiotemporal forecasting use case, with accuracy and computational savings still to be assessed from the full paper.
visual_elements: Des Plaines River watershed map with a zoom-in illustrating the 30 m prediction grid.

paper_title: Flood forecasting using a physics-guided conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model
paper_authors: Omar Sallam, David Coe, Jeremy Feinstein, Hugo Torres, Sofia Sahagun Covarrubias
